response:
Innate Immunity Components:
- Inflammatory response
- Phagocytes (monocytes, granulocytes, neutrophils)
- Complement
- Cytokines, chemokines, and anti-microbial peptides (AMPs)
- Natural Killer cells

Diseases linked to Innate Immunity defects:
- Complement defects (e.g. C3) linked to autoimmune diseases like lupus
- Complement non-core defects linked to susceptibility to specific pathogens
- Macrophage deficiencies like Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD) linked to bacterial infection
- Macrophage deficiencies with IRF8 mutations linked to TB susceptibility
- Aicardi-Goutières syndrome linked to inflammatory cytokine production
- Lack of interferon-responsiveness linked to viral infection like COVID-19

Comparison of Innate and Adaptive Immunity:
- Cell types: Macrophages, neutrophils, DCs vs. Lymphocytes
- Speed: Fast vs. Slow
- Memory: No vs. Yes
- Specificity: Low vs. High
- Receptors: Pattern Recognition vs. TCR/Ig
- Strategy of recognition: Few highly conserved microbial ligands vs. Randomly generated receptors for billions of possible antigens
